messages.text: A and I both want the trailer in the next few weeks, and neither of us is backing down. B's pad is where it lives, so she is stuck in the middle. Can you help the three of us sort this out?

It’s been fine, mostly, but the trailer does take up space behind my house, and I’d rather it weren’t there. I feel a bit awkward saying that because I agreed to the arrangement with you both and don’t want to let you down. I’d feel better with a clear plan to move it, but I rent, so my landlord would need to approve any change to what’s kept on the pad. I haven’t asked him yet, so I’m not sure what he’d say.

I need it for hauling materials for my home project, and it needs to happen in the next few weeks. I’m not willing to wait until A is done using it. My concern is that we haven’t settled how access and decisions work when we all own it but it’s stored at B’s.

I want the trailer for weekend trips starting in the next few weeks. If it’s not available, I’ll miss those trips; I don’t have a specific dollar cost in mind. My main concern is shared decisions dragging out access—I want to be able to plan my trips without a lot of back-and-forth.

That’s close. I’d say I’d like it moved off the pad without feeling I’m letting you both down. I’d be willing to ask my landlord informally; I just haven’t yet. I’d rather it live elsewhere, though occasional visits might be fine.
Mostly, but it’s *her* project. The next-few-weeks timing isn’t tied to a fixed delivery or crew; I just need it soon, and I won’t wait until A is done. I didn’t know B wanted the trailer moved.

That wording mostly fits, but don’t call it a fixed deadline: I need it in the next few weeks, and I won’t just wait for A. There isn’t a more specific reason. If B wants it moved, we need to discuss another storage spot.
Yes, that fits. I’d rather ask my landlord myself when I’m ready, but thank you for offering.

Mostly. I’m she, and I want to plan my trips without negotiating every use. I don’t know if C’s project conflicts; if it can be scheduled around my weekends, sharing could work. I’d need the trailer for my trips, though. I hadn’t heard B wanted it gone, and that does concern me.
Worth checking the actual dates, yes. But “won’t go second” overstates it: I need to use it soon, not simply wait until A is done. We haven’t established that our dates actually clash.

Not quite. What worries me is that B would rather the trailer weren’t there, and I don’t want that to leave me without it for my trips. I don’t know what happens next, so I can’t say more than that. And yes, C and I haven’t established a date clash.

A and C seem useful for sorting out actual clashes over use. B gives me room to ask my landlord when I’m ready, which I appreciate, but it doesn’t yet address my main wish: for the trailer to move off my pad. I’m not sure what’s allowed until I ask him, so I’d want that handled separately without holding up the dates.
